Verse image generator

You’re already welcome here—make one card or only preview; sharing never buys your place.

Build a calm, share-ready KJV card—start with a dawn template (square, story, or print) or stay on the wide custom canvas. Export PNG or share from your device; no upload required.

Gentle roadmap (verse images v2)

No hype, no rush—these are the next calm upgrades we are working toward. Everything stays KJV, offline-friendly, and pressure-free. Deep link: verse-image.html?ref=John%203:16 (optional &autoload=1 to load text + preview). v2 line balance on canvas: ?vi_v2=1 and Update preview.

  • Smarter line breaks — Poetic KJV phrasing, fewer orphans on tall templates.
  • Size presets in one tap — Lock to square, story, or slide without guesswork.
  • Font pairs that stay readable — Titles and verse body tuned for small screens and print.
  • Optional batch for series — Same style across a short plan, still gentle (no “productivity” language).
University of God — calm background prompts (copy to your image model)

Use with your own generator—no hype, KJV-true tone, soft dawn palette (slate, mist gold, still water). Add “no text, no legible words” in your model if it tends to print letters. University of God is not a place of pressure; the art should read room to breathe, learn, return.

Open stone doorway at first light, empty lectern, single oil lamp, gentle fog—invitation, not a crowd.

Calm map table with a folded scroll, quill, small compass, ocean-mist haze—Christ as compass point.

Row of arched windows in an old study hall, rain on glass, warm lamp pools on an open book—quiet school in storm.

Path through wheat toward a thin golden horizon, one figure in silhouette (small, humble)—daily lesson on the way home.

Cliff top bench overlooking sea at dawn, empty seat, gulls far off—secret prayer, wind as friend not threat.

Two small garden paths at grey dawn, same rain on both, mists, low wildflowers—no scoreboard, no faces; University of Comparison mood: enough, not parade; no legible app text, no “winning” signs.

Open window at dusk, empty chair, glass of water, Bible closed on sill, last cool light—University of Anger mood: heat leaving the room, no shouting figures, no readable screens; indigo to pale gold.

Child-sized desk with crayons, open Psalms, tiny globe, light shaft—children’s classroom, joy without noise.

Stack of course booklets with linen covers, olive branch, wax seal (blank)—Battle plans as gentle companions, not a badge.

Library ladder in half-light, KJV-shelf mood (no legible spines), single bookmark ribbon—Word as lamp, next step only.

Hand reaching down to help someone up a grassy slope, soft focus faces—fear and anxiety class: accompany, not fix.

Empty chapel chairs in semicircle, one stem of wildflowers, sun through dust—grief and waiting, room for tears and hope.

Shaded porch, wooden swing, glass of water and closed book on a side table—summer stillness, heat without noise, no pool party, no people-pleasing; room to be still before the day runs.

Lakeside dock at mid-morning, still water, one bird mid-flight, soft gold haze—Summer in the University mood: same gentle school, new light, Christ as quiet companion (no legible text).

Harvest table, loaf, simple bowl, wheat stalks, low candle, linen cloth—thanksgiving that names the Giver, not a feast flex; warm ink-friendly tones, no readable words on paper props.

Dawn kitchen window, steam from a mug, open Bible on counter, child-height chair empty—Family Armor morning reset: new mercies, small hands soon to come, hush before the rush (no text on mug).

Field edge at deep twilight, fireflies, single hay bale, long grass—late summer hush, questions and hope in the same sky; no people, no party lights; warm-not-neon gold.

Small orchard, ladder leaning on one tree, basket of apples on grass, long harvest shadows—thanksgiving that names the Giver; no readable crate labels, no people required.

Wheat stubble at sundown, one sheaf tied with twine, crow far off—quiet fall harvest, Psalm-shaped joy after tears, no parade; warm ochre, no text on burlap.

Barn door half open, last light, empty bushel, brass lantern (no label), dust-motes—the floor full later; thanks before the count; ink-friendly, no legible signs.

Grape arbor turning red-gold, snips on a wood crate, one cluster left for the sparrows—gleaning humbles the eye, joy without the flex; KJV-calm palette.

Creek under turning maples, mist, two stones for sitting, thermos and closed Bible on a check wool blanket—fall praise outside performance; no faces; no brand marks.

Kitchen table before dawn, single mug, modest plate, curtains half-drawn, crumbs on linen—Contentment in small seasons mood: warm paper white, restrained gold, no parade; no faces; tiny optional KJV marginalia only (“Sufficient unto the day” Matthew 6:34 or “I will never leave thee” Hebrews 13:5); no app UI.

Counter stack of mail and school papers slightly out of focus, one cleared corner with open Bible and pen, cool blue hour light—Contentment in small seasons: ordinary weight, quiet mercy; no faces, no legible addresses; ink-friendly blues and sand.

Windowsill herbs in small pots, watering can, rain on glass, empty chair at the table behind—small things honored; muted sage, grey, gold rim; no people; optional tiny KJV line from Zechariah 4:10 about the day of small things—not legible app text.

Desk edge at night, three sticky notes half curling, lamp low, glass of water—University of Overwhelm mood: too many threads, one hush of light; indigo to warm sand; no faces; no readable screen pixels; optional tiny KJV from Psalm 142:3 (“thou knewest my path”) in margin only.

Foggy porch steps, one anchor rope coiled on rail, still air—too much at once, but something holds; University of Overwhelm palette; no storm worship, no people; optional tiny KJV from Matthew 11:28 (“Come unto me”) as whisper-small margin text.

Soft morning light through a kitchen window onto a plain table: a few scattered toys, open Bible, steaming mug beside—University of Overwhelm in daylight hours; muted blues and greys, warm ceramic; no faces; optional tiny Matthew 11:28 line (“Come unto me”) in margin only; no packaging text, no app UI.

Hallway night-light glow, two small shoes by the door, jacket on hook, empty frame for silhouette (no faces)—Fear for my children mood: vigil without doom-scroll; soft amber, deep blue; optional tiny KJV from Matthew 18:14 about the Father’s will toward little ones—no legible feeds.

Backseat of parked car at dusk, empty booster silhouette, rain on window, streetlights soft bokeh—prayer before pickup energy; University fear-for-children mood; no readable plates; muted steel blue and gold; optional tiny KJV from Isaiah 54:13 (“great shall be the peace of thy children”) in margin.

Gentle nursery corner at twilight, small empty bed, closed Bible on a nightstand, one soft lamp—Fear for my children mood; linen and dusk blue, no faces; optional tiny KJV from Psalm 91:11 (“he shall give his angels charge over thee”) as whisper margin only; no glowing screens, no legible monitors.

Your card

One-tap size

When on, changing the template does not resize the canvas (colors and layout still follow the template you pick).

Same-mood template picks (lazy; tap a swatch)

Calm color hints — the full render still uses the canvas. Opens fast on slow connections because swatches are CSS only.

Points to a short link on this site so people can open the verse after a meeting. Handouts work best when someone has opened the site once before (cache helps).

Leave it on for story shares and handouts; turn it off if you need a cleaner print-ready card.
